text:
Diego (Acme): hey team, our overnight batch (job: batch-emb-50k) hit 0 credits mid-run and now the API returns 429 even though it’s past midnight for our tenant. UI still shows 0. We expected a refill at 00:00 CEST. Any idea?
Samantha (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste the tenant id and the job id + approx timestamps? also which region/timezone is the tenant set to?
Diego (Acme): tenant: acme-prod-3, job: batch-emb-50k, started 2024-11-03T22:15:00+02:00, observed 429 ~2024-11-04T00:02:30+02:00. Tenant timezone CEST. We retried a few times and still got 429s.
Samantha (Support): thanks — tagging billing and infra. @Maya can you confirm if the monthly refill recorded for acme-prod-3 at 00:00 CEST or if any prorate/plan change happened?
Maya (Billing): pulling records now. On our side tenancy shows a scheduled monthly refill at 2024-11-04T00:00:00Z (00:00 UTC). No plan change or proration logged recently. Refill job marked successful at 00:00 UTC for tenant acme-prod-3.
Samantha (Support): ok billing confirms refill job succeeded at 00:00 UTC. @Kai can infra check if the cache/quotas service propagated the new tokens to the API layer? sometimes cache sticky keys delay visibility.
Kai (SRE): looking. I see the refill event hit the billing db at 00:00Z but the quota cache (redis slot: quotas:acme-prod-3) last updated 2024-11-03T23:58:00Z and I don’t see the 00:00Z write propagated to the cache due to a partial outage on the cache cluster between 00:00-00:01Z. ops-bot shows: "partial write failure -> retry queued".
ops-bot: cache-cluster-a: partial write failure at 2024-11-04T00:00:50Z, retries pending.
Kai (SRE): can you paste one sample 429 response header from your client, Diego? need to confirm whether header shows wallet/token counts.
Diego (Acme): here’s an example returned by our SDK:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-retry-after: 30
x-tenant-credits-remaining: 0
x-tenant-credits-window-reset: 170, 0
```
Samantha (Support): perfect — confirms API layer saw zero. I’m going to ask infra to flush the quota cache key after billing confirms refill record (to force reload). @Maya confirmed billing write was successful.
Kai (SRE): executing cache flush: `redis-cli -c -h cache-cluster-a del quotas:acme-prod-3` -> returned 1. For safety I also triggered `quota-service --recompute --tenant acme-prod-3`.
Kai (SRE): can you retry the same request?
Diego (Acme): retrying now... results: success! 200 and tokens restored. UI still shows 0 on the account page, though.
Samantha (Support): thanks Diego — that matches: service layer token pool is restored but UI (frontend cache / CDN) is still showing stale value. @Maya can you confirm if any UI cache invalidation ran?
Maya (Billing): frontend cache is on a separate CDN tier; no automatic purge on refill. I’ve queued a CDN purge for tenant account page cache (should propagate in ~2-3min).
Diego (Acme): UI updated after ~2 minutes. All good now. Appreciate the quick triage.
Samantha (Support): summary for records: root cause was quota cache write retries during a brief cache-cluster partial outage at refill time; billing refill succeeded but quota cache wasn’t updated, causing API to continue returning 429 until manual cache flush + recompute. Action items: 1) Kai to add retry/backoff metrics and alert for quota cache write failures, 2) infra to add a short-lived reconciliation job after refill to ensure caches are authoritative, 3) support KB update with guidance for customers running large batch jobs about staggering concurrency to avoid draining visible buckets.
Kai (SRE): noted — will file infra ticket and follow up with runbook changes.
Maya (Billing): I’ll add a small note in billing runbook that refill success should trigger cache reconciliation hook.
Samantha (Support): closing the immediate support ticket. Diego if anything else pops up DM me and we’ll reopen. :thumbsup:
